properties.decision:
**Anthony's word, 2026-08-26: park it.** Option (e) of `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built`.

📌 DISTINCT FROM THAT NODE BY ROLE, NOT BY WORDING, AND THE ID IS LOAD-BEARING. That one is the DELIBERATION — the open question, its five options and the argument on each. This is the RULING, and it must carry exactly this id because `vocabulary_coverage` looks the domain's `park_with` up by it. A ruling a machine reads and a deliberation a person reads are different artifacts; merging them would leave the tool with nothing to find.

WHAT IS PARKED: the compliance half of the `environment` domain — the `EnvironmentRule` node type and the `IMPOSES`, `COMPLIES_WITH` and `VIOLATES_RULE` edges. Declared in `schema/environment.yaml` since 2026-07-17, zero instances, zero typed tools, zero instructions, zero detectors.

WHAT IS **NOT** PARKED, and the distinction matters: the LOCATING half of the same domain is live and working — `Environment` (3 instances, written by `add_environment`) and `DEPLOYED_TO` (63 edges, written by `deploy_to`). `OPERATES_IN` sits between them: 3 live edges, no tool. **Parking is not retirement and touches none of these.**

═══ WHY PARK RATHER THAN BUILD ═══

Three field reports this month — hxm_program, Alex, and the storyflow fleet — mention environment compliance **zero times**. Building a fully-specified but unrequested subsystem is answering a question the schema asked rather than one a user did, which is the over-engineering failure mode this project measures itself against.

Parking is the only disposition that costs nothing to reverse. A parked domain a user later asks for becomes a build with nothing undone; a subsystem built unrequested cannot be un-built and adds surface every future session reads past.

═══ WHY NOT RETIRE ═══

Retiring was on the table as option (c) and is now known to be partly destructive: it would remove `OPERATES_IN`, which carries live edges in this design. The design is also sound — the three-way distinction between `Constraint` (self-imposed), `DesignRule` (chosen convention) and `EnvironmentRule` (externally imposed, negotiable only by variance or waiver) is good vocabulary, and the `VIOLATES_RULE` lifecycle where `confirmed` means an accepted variance kept and documented is better thought through than much of what ships.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS ═══

**A user asking.** Specifically: any design in a regulated operating environment where an external authority imposes a ruleset the design can only comply with, seek a variance from, or fail. Brookhaven NSLS-II and Space Force acquisition both look like that from the outside, and neither has reached for it.

📌 AND ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY, kept at full strength because it is the only thing on that side. `OPERATES_IN` has three edges and no tool writes them — an earlier session reached for the vocabulary and fell through to raw `create_edge`, the escape hatch the three-legs rule says must not count as reachability. That is thin, it came from inside the project rather than from a user, and it was judged insufficient to justify building. If it recurs — especially from a consumer rather than from us — this parking should be revisited rather than defended.
properties.name: PARKED — the environment compliance vocabulary is deliberately unused until a user asks for it
properties.rationale:
Recorded as the domain's `park_with` ruling, which is the node `vocabulary_coverage` already names for this purpose: accepting it declares the domain deliberately unused, so unused environment vocabulary stops reading as a hole in every coverage report without anything being deleted.

That is the same principle as `ruling: parks` one layer down and the same principle as `dec:idea-a-proposed-decision-asserts-nothing-...` one layer up: a deliberate state must be COUNTED and explained rather than either reported as a defect or silently hidden. All three exist because a count that grows when somebody does the right thing teaches people to stop reading it.

The agent recommended parking and Anthony took it. The counter-evidence — three `OPERATES_IN` edges written through the escape hatch — is recorded on the decision rather than dropped, because it is the one fact that would justify overturning this and it should not have to be rediscovered.
